found.title: File:Drover's Arms Inn on Epynt mountain - geograph.org.uk - 157616.jpg
found.desc: Drover's Arms Inn on Epynt mountain Long ago this was a real inn. It was purchased by the War Office in 1940 as part of the military training ground and artillery range that now surrounds it. The outer shell was restored 1994 but inside it is a shelter for soldiers not a pub. It has an authentic looking pub sign but instead of the brewery name it reads "Ministry of Defence".

found.title: File:House at Ffrwd-wen on Epynt mountain - geograph.org.uk - 157607.jpg
found.desc: House at Ffrwd-wen on Epynt mountain I suspect that this isn't a real house - nothing is what it seems to be in this military training area. Everything is surrounded by signs telling you you're going to be blown up if you walk out onto the grass, but the sheep don't seem to care.

found.title: File:Road crosses stream on Epynt mountain - geograph.org.uk - 157601.jpg
found.desc: Road crosses stream on Epynt mountain The red flags are flying today, so I'm limited to pictures at the roadside on this artillery range.

found.title: File:Stop sign on B4519 near Upper Chapel - geograph.org.uk - 157647.jpg
found.desc: Stop sign on B4519 near Upper Chapel As this road runs northwest into the Epynt mountain it passes through Sennybridge artillery range. This sign is used to stop traffic when weapons fire makes it unsafe to drive.

found.title: File:Stop sign on road north of Epynt mountain - geograph.org.uk - 157581.jpg
found.desc: Stop sign on road north of Epynt mountain Travelling southeast from Garth to Brecon will take you over the Sennybridge military training facility's artillery range on the Epynt mountain. These signs are used to stop traffic when weapons fire makes it unsafe to drive. Judging by the lack of a line over the pulley used to raise the disc it would seem that this sign is seldom used.

found.title: File:Motor Rallying on Epynt Ranges - geograph.org.uk - 392723.jpg
found.desc: Motor Rallying on Epynt Ranges The Epynt Ranges are a regular venue for motor rallying. This photo was taken at the 2006 Wales Rally GB

found.title: File:Into the danger zone - geograph.org.uk - 468892.jpg
found.desc: Into the danger zone The road south across the training area on the Epynt mountain starts here near Tirabad. Don't turn off onto any of the military's lanes.

found.title: File:"S" is for "sheep" - geograph.org.uk - 816487.jpg
found.desc: "S" is for "sheep" The sheep roam freely through the area. The S is one of the marker signs for the artillery range.

found.title: File:Entrance to SENTA - geograph.org.uk - 816089.jpg
found.desc: Entrance to SENTA SENTA, the Sennybridge Training Area, is a large area of land on and around Mynydd Epynt used for army training. This is one of the entrances off the B4520 and was formerly a public road across the moors.

found.title: File:Epynt training area - geograph.org.uk - 815606.jpg
found.desc: Epynt training area Some of the many copses of trees planted for training purposes can be seen here, with open moorland between.

found.title: File:Epynt training area near Cae'n-y-waun - geograph.org.uk - 815613.jpg
found.desc: Epynt training area near Cae'n-y-waun Towards the northern edge of the army training area. There are plenty of stands of planted trees.

found.title: File:From the Brynhynae bridleway - geograph.org.uk - 814840.jpg
found.desc: From the Brynhynae bridleway A bridleway runs south-west to north-east through the square, out of the Mynydd Epynt army training area. This is looking south towards the restricted area, clearly seen above the fields.

found.title: File:Looking into the Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 815627.jpg
found.desc: Looking into the Epynt From a bridleway that runs from Brynhynae, this is the point where it enters the Epynt army training area. The bridleway is still shown on the map although the army do not encourage its use but instead promote the Epynt Way which is joined here.

found.title: File:Mynydd Epynt training area - geograph.org.uk - 814898.jpg
found.desc: Mynydd Epynt training area This picture covers most of the southern half of the square, and shows the typical moorland terrain.

found.title: File:Mynydd Epynt training area - geograph.org.uk - 816475.jpg
found.desc: Mynydd Epynt training area The eastern side of the area, with two of the many stands of trees both in the square.

found.title: File:Red kite viewing area - geograph.org.uk - 815545.jpg
found.desc: Red kite viewing area This small car park by the south-eastern cattle grid on the B4519 is promoted by the army as a red kite viewing area. In practice it is a good view as well over some of the Mynydd Epynt artillery range, with the wooded areas on the hill being clearly shown on the map in SN9842. The plaque explains the creation of the Epynt Way, a circular footpath round the perimeter of the Mynydd Epynt army training area. The map clearly shows its route and the no-go areas.

found.title: File:On Mynydd Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 826098.jpg
found.desc: On Mynydd Epynt This stand of trees is close to the highest point of the Mynydd Epynt. This square is all part of the military training area, and I am standing adjacent to the access barrier to one of the observation points.

found.title: File:Cwm above Troedyrhiw - geograph.org.uk - 838155.jpg
found.desc: Cwm above Troedyrhiw One of the steep cwms off the north-western scarp face of Mynydd Epynt.

found.title: File:Disgwylfa visitor centre - geograph.org.uk - 839775.jpg
found.desc: Disgwylfa visitor centre A former farm building, the centre has a small museum and information about the natural environment of the Mynydd Epynt. So the web site says anyway; I've been there three times so far and it has been shut every time.

found.title: File:On reflection, it's OK - geograph.org.uk - 839534.jpg
found.desc: On reflection, it's OK The edge of the Mynydd Epynt army training area and a danger flag is flying. But you are allowed to enter as far as the Epynt Way, about 30 feet in where that sheep is. First there's a pool to cross though. Oh, another red flag!

found.title: File:Road across the moors - geograph.org.uk - 839690.jpg
found.desc: Road across the moors The B4519 is clearly seen winding across the moors through the various parts of the Mynydd Epynt army training area. Once a remote moorland road, this route is probably more used since the army came in than before.

found.title: File:Training use only - geograph.org.uk - 839632.jpg
found.desc: Training use only One of a group of houses constructed by the army in the training area, and probably used as barracks.

found.title: File:Moorland on Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1013499.jpg
found.desc: Moorland on Epynt Couch grass can be seen in the foreground of this shot of moorland on Epynt.

found.title: File:Moorland on Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1013507.jpg
found.desc: Moorland on Epynt Small stream making its way off moorland on Epynt.

found.title: File:Stile to Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1013516.jpg
found.desc: Stile to Epynt Stile for a permissive footpath that leads from Cwm-Llythin to Epynt.

found.title: File:Epynt rally stage - geograph.org.uk - 1126338.jpg
found.desc: Epynt rally stage The shot was taken while I was spectating at the Epynt rally stage of the Wales Rally GB and shows the view across the countryside with a Subaru competitor in action

found.title: File:Above Nant Bran - geograph.org.uk - 1179924.jpg
found.desc: Above Nant Bran From the military road, looking towards the common impact area of the higher Epynt moorland. This road is not often open to the public but a motor rally was taking place there this weekend.

found.title: File:Across Mynydd Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1179778.jpg
found.desc: Across Mynydd Epynt This army route follows the former drove road across the moorland. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:Approach to Mynydd Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1173464.jpg
found.desc: Approach to Mynydd Epynt The flag is a general one marking the limit of the military training area. The square is mainly rough grazing, planted stands of trees and lower level pasture.

found.title: File:Drove road across the Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1178377.jpg
found.desc: Drove road across the Epynt The path is very easy to follow across the moorland, although there is frequent evidence of artillery targets on the moorland.

found.title: File:Drove road across the Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1179775.jpg
found.desc: Drove road across the Epynt Part of the edge of the road, showing significant erosion of the peat over the years. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:Drove road across the Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1179777.jpg
found.desc: Drove road across the Epynt The drove road turns more to the south, left, here but the other track is also a one-time significant route to the Mynydd Bwlch-y-Groes area. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:Former Epynt drove road - geograph.org.uk - 1178355.jpg
found.desc: Former Epynt drove road This path across the training area is the former drove road across the Mynydd Epynt, sticking to the higher ground. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:Former Epynt drove road - geograph.org.uk - 1178407.jpg
found.desc: Former Epynt drove road The line of the former drove road can be picked out most of the way, sticking to the higher ground across the Epynt. It is easy to follow and there is evidence of recent vehicle use. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:Mynydd Epynt observation post - geograph.org.uk - 1173460.jpg
found.desc: Mynydd Epynt observation post The trig point is at 409 metres, and is one of five around the edges of the Mynydd Epynt plateau at strategic locations. It is also one of the observation posts, used by military commanders to check progress with manoeuvres, the modern equivalent of the general on horseback. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:South from Crug Du - geograph.org.uk - 1179818.jpg
found.desc: South from Crug Du Rough grazing on the moorland plateau. The wall enclosing the former fields of Blaenegnant-uchaf can be seen. The stand of trees on the right horizon is at SN952385. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down.

found.title: File:Strata above Nant Talar - geograph.org.uk - 1178413.jpg
found.desc: Strata above Nant Talar An exposed section of the soil shows its composition, old red sandstone and mudstone.

found.title: File:Tour of Epynt rally - geograph.org.uk - 1176688.jpg
found.desc: Tour of Epynt rally This is on a military road through the south of the training area. This road is not often open to the public but a motor rally was taking place there this weekend and the car is on its reconnaissance trip for the race the following day. The area is mainly rough grazing.

found.title: File:Track on Mynydd Epynt - geograph.org.uk - 1173401.jpg
found.desc: Track on Mynydd Epynt This is a track that used to be the old Llywel to Tirabad road, but which has been moved to the west of a military range. The area is not often open to the public but it is a non-firing day and the red flags are down. However, the barrier is still down so I didn't explore further.

found.title: File:Welsh TT races Trophy.jpg
found.desc: Welsh TT Trophy on display at Camarthen Museum

found.title: File:Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 157640.jpg
found.desc: Epynt Way The red flag in the background indicates it is not safe to walk on the grass but the notice on the finger post states that this is the Epynt Way and that it is always safe to walk it.

found.title: File:Buildings at Pwll Du on the Sennybridge training area - geograph.org.uk - 791192.jpg
found.desc: Buildings at Pwll Du on the Sennybridge training area From the Epynt way a house and shed are visible at the head of a track up this small valley. The buildings straddle the meeting point of four grid squares.

found.title: File:Epynt Way leg 6 and boundary fence - geograph.org.uk - 790153.jpg
found.desc: Epynt Way leg 6 and boundary fence Looking back down the fence line towards the starting point of leg 6 of the Epynt Way. It starts at the car parkon the main Llywel road that crosses behind the buildings in the distance. The Epynt Way runs around the MOD Sennybridge Training Area, mostly on the MOD land just inside the perimeter fence. Any fence that separates civilian land from the danger area has red discs attached.

found.title: File:Epynt Way marker ^625 - geograph.org.uk - 790161.jpg
found.desc: Epynt Way marker #625 While travelling anticlockwise around the ascending numbered marker posts, don't forget to look behind you occasionally. At the top of this ascent you get a great view of the Bannau (pictured) or even the Brecon Beacons.

found.title: File:Plantation corner on the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 790164.jpg
found.desc: Plantation corner on the Epynt Way Marker post 628 is right on the corner of this small plantation. Two sheep are sheltering from the wind under the overhanging branches. This plantation is not shown on the 50K map but does appear on the 25K.

found.title: File:From the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 814805.jpg
found.desc: From the Epynt Way The way passes legitimately through the army training area. There are many of these tree covers planted especially for training purposes.

found.title: File:No way in - geograph.org.uk - 816065.jpg
found.desc: No way in This fence and its sign make it clear, you cannot follow the former footpath past here. The Epynt Way makes its way through the training area in front of the stand of woodland, but you have to be in there to get there.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 815556.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way A long distance path has been created roughly around the perimeter of the Mynydd Epynt army training area. This is looking north near the eastern side of the square.

found.title: File:Mabioin Way monument - geograph.org.uk - 826077.jpg
found.desc: Mabioin Way monument This was constructed in 1973 to mark the completion of the Mabioin Way (the army training area perimeter road) by the Royal Engineers.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 826061.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The Epynt Way runs around the perimeter of the army training area. On this section the old moorland path runs parallel to a newer military road.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 826067.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The way runs parallel to the Mabbions Way military road on the north-west edge of the Epynt scarp.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 826262.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The Epynt Way runs within the army training area, close to the perimeter. It is usually open for walkers and horse-riders, even when the red flags are flying. Here is a section descending towards the Blaen Dunhonw. The woodland is at SN986463 and virtually everything else in the picture is in the square.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 837631.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way A bit wet in places, but generally an excellent path along the north-western scarp of the Mynydd Epynt, legitimately just within the army training area.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 837654.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The way follows the old moorland track, below the new army road.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 837683.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The way runs parallel to Mabbions Way along the scarp crest of the Mynydd Epynt. The vehicle in the middle distance is in the square and is that of a marshall for the motor rally taking place in the Crychan forest to the right.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 839555.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The way skirts round the northern edge of the training area on this clearly defined track. It runs for 55 miles, mainly around the perimeter of the army training area.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 839579.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The way stays close to the boundary of the army training area here, and crosses a couple of steep-sided small streams, such as this one. The bridleway option heads further to the right to a more gentle crossing.

found.title: File:Entering the Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 985807.jpg
found.desc: Entering the Sennybridge Training Area Here the B4519 enters the Sennybridge Training Area.

found.title: File:On the Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 1173426.jpg
found.desc: On the Epynt Way The Epynt Way is a long distance path providing a circuit of the military training area. Here is one of the information boards as the way crosses the Cilieni and low lying sheep pasture.

found.title: File:The Epynt Way - geograph.org.uk - 1175806.jpg
found.desc: The Epynt Way The Epynt Way is a long distance footpath and bridleway that encircles the Sennybridge training area, usually just inside the boundary. It is accessible at all times. From this point where it cross the road above Llandeilo'r-Fan the first objective is over the shoulder of that hill and down into Cwm Mawan beyond. The full route is 75 kilometres, 47 miles, 21 hours walking.

found.desc: Oak chair won by Iorwerth C. Peate at the Student Eisteddfod held in Aberystwyth in 1921. The chair has the signature of the wood-carver, Emile De Vynck, on the back. He was a Belgian refuguee who came to Wales from Mechelen during the First World War. De Vynck and his family, along with other Belgians, were given refuge by Lloyd George in Pentrefelin, north Wales. He made other eisteddfod chairs and carved wooden pieces which have remained in the area.

found.title: File:Fake village in Sennybridge training area - geograph.org.uk - 448067.jpg
found.desc: Fake village in Sennybridge training area Sennybridge M.O.D training area is a huge area of the Epynt Mountain. All you can normally see from the two public roads crossing it are small military sheds and dirt roads. This is apparently an entire village constructed for military training purposes.

found.title: File:Narrow bridge in Sennybridge training area - geograph.org.uk - 468894.jpg
found.desc: Narrow bridge in Sennybridge training area Although the military would prefer you not to dawdle along this public road across their training area, there are several bottlenecks where you may have to wait to let traffic pass.

found.title: File:Road through Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 475477.jpg
found.desc: Road through Sennybridge Training Area A narrow road with passing places crosses the danger area. Don't stop for a picnic - they may want to clear the road for a spot of artillery shelling.

found.title: File:Cattle grid on border of Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 790177.jpg
found.desc: Cattle grid on border of Sennybridge Training Area The public road from the Pentrebach on the A40 through the Halfway Forest crosses into the danger area over this cattle grid.

found.title: File:Junction on road through Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 790169.jpg
found.desc: Junction on road through Sennybridge Training Area A side track branches off from the public road that leaves SENTA through the Halfway Forest.

found.title: File:Plantation beside public road in Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 790173.jpg
found.desc: Plantation beside public road in Sennybridge Training Area You are not allowed to park up and wander off from the public roads that cross the danger area. Often the only significant features are the small geometric shaped plantations.

found.title: File:Footpath direction post in Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 945321.jpg
found.desc: Footpath direction post in Sennybridge Training Area Here, on the edge of Sennybridge Training Area, is a sign showing path crossing junction, the northerly path is marked as no entry (danger area).

found.title: File:Military road leading from firing range - Sennybridge Training Area - geograph.org.uk - 945289.jpg

found.title: File:Babell chapel - geograph.org.uk - 1176161.jpg
found.desc: Babell chapel This is the site of Babell chapel, the main religious and community site when the Mynydd Epynt was populated. There are still gravestones here, although main structure of the chapel itself has not survived. Services of repentance are held here from time to time by Cymdeithas y Cymod, the Welsh branch of the International Fellowship of Reconciliation. This area is not often open to the public but a motor rally was taking place there this weekend.

found.title: File:Moorland near Cefn-bryn - geograph.org.uk - 1176255.jpg

found.title: File:Over the Cilieni - geograph.org.uk - 1176101.jpg
found.desc: Over the Cilieni This bridge takes this minor road over the Cilieni, a river that drains much of the western section of the Sennybridge training area yet looks still remarkably small here.

found.title: File:Over the watershed - geograph.org.uk - 1177362.jpg
found.desc: Over the watershed This low lying wet moorland is the watershed between the Afon Dulas flowing north (left) into the Wye river system and the Cilieni flowing south (right) into the Usk river system. The watershed is followed by the Llywel to Tirabad road then a drove road for the whole length of the army training area. Behind, in SN8938 is Cilieni, a fake village used for fighting in a built up area (FIBUA) training.
